The app is built, verified, and ready for you to try.

## Your bookmark app is ready to review

**Open → http://maker:4000**
**Sign in:** email **`demo@bookmarks.test`**, password **`demo123`** — or click **"Create an account"** to make your own (your real personal account, reachable from any device).

### What it does — exactly the 13 flows we agreed
- **Sign in** to your own central collection; **sign out** top-right; your bookmarks persist between visits and across devices.
- **Save a link** — details fill in automatically (from the real page), editable; add **tags** as chips with one-click reuse, and a **personal note**.
- If a page's details can't be fetched, you can **still type a title and save**; an invalid link is explained and blocked.
- Saving a link you already have **doesn't duplicate** — it takes you to the existing one, opened for editing.
- **Live search** as you type across titles, descriptions, notes, links and tags, spanning **To read** and **Finished**; click a tag to filter.
- **To read / Finished** tabs; **Archive** to hide-but-keep (out of normal search, in its own tab, restorable with its status intact); **Delete** for good, with confirmation.
- Every bookmark fully editable: web address, title, description, note, tags, status.

### Verification report (plain language)
I checked the app against every one of the 13 approved behaviours and it passes:
- **9 automated acceptance checks** driving a real browser — sign-in/rejection, saving with auto-fill/tags/note, invalid-link and fetch-failure handling, live search across fields and tabs, tag filtering, finished/archive/restore, duplicate handling, editing with address validation and collision-blocking, delete confirmation, and persistence after sign-out.
- **35 internal tests** covering the link/duplicate rules, metadata parsing, password security, and all data operations with per-account isolation.

All 44 pass. Passwords are stored hashed (never in plain text). A couple of items we agreed were *not* part of this build are noted for later: performance tuning for very large collections, and cross-device sync latency.

**Do you accept this software as meeting the behaviour we approved, completing this first cycle?** If anything doesn't behave as we agreed, tell me and I'll correct it within this cycle; if it's a new idea beyond what we approved, I'll record it for a future cycle.
